nodes.label: Log-return target formulation
nodes.rationale: TARGET='Close' predicts the price level; for a near-random-walk series the persistence baseline is near-optimal by construction, so the reported -23.5% skill was roughly what the formulation predicts a priori, largely independent of hyperparameters. Modelling r[t]=log(C[t]/C[t-1]) makes the baseline 'predict zero return' (beatable), makes the band scale-free and comparable across symbols, stops GroupNormalizer fighting a non-stationary level, and makes pooling sensible. Measured: skill -59.5% to +2.4% (+3.8% purged) on identical data/seed/epochs. Default deliberately left at 'close' because effective n about 5 is not enough to flip a default and invalidate every existing bundle.

nodes.label: Persistence baseline
nodes.rationale: Predict the last observed close (or zero return under the log-return target). Introduced by PYQ-201 because model quality had been reported only as an absolute QuantileLoss with nothing to compare against; it is the only baseline in the project until PYQ-249 lands.

nodes.label: Walk-forward backtest geometry
nodes.rationale: One 5-day held-out window per symbol is too small and high-variance to drive EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint selection; rolling origins with disjoint evaluation windows aggregate PYQ-201's metrics across many origins instead.

nodes.label: Conformalized quantile regression (CQR)
nodes.rationale: Score max(q_lo - y, y - q_hi) on a held-out calibration slice, take the finite-sample corrected quantile ceil((n+1)*coverage)/n, and widen or narrow the band by that amount. Chosen because it is distribution-free, needs no retraining or loss change, is about 80 lines, and composes with the existing quantile head. Only the outer quantiles move: shifting the median would change the reported direction with no evidence for it. The guarantee assumes exchangeability, which financial series violate, so it is paired with purged splits and achieved coverage is reported rather than assumed. Defaults to off (calibration_days=0) because switching it on silently changes every reported coverage figure.

nodes.label: Purge and embargo around splits
nodes.rationale: Lopez de Prado's treatment: drop training samples whose label window overlaps the test window (purge) plus a buffer after it (embargo), because serial correlation leaks across the boundary. The actual leak here is not decoder-to-decoder overlap but that a validation sample's encoder reads max_encoder_length days that are training targets. Measured skill rose rather than fell, which at effective n about 5 is read as inside the noise, establishing only that purging is not catastrophic to fit quality.

nodes.label: Effective sample size under overlapping windows
nodes.rationale: Windows built with min_prediction_idx=cutoff+1 overlap heavily (consecutive windows share 4 of 5 target days), so a raw count of 280 predictions overstates independent evidence by roughly the horizon; a CI computed as if n=280 is about sqrt(5)x too narrow. Reporting effective n is what stopped PYQ-247's ~62-point skill improvement being written up as settled.
nodes.norm_label: effective sample size under overlapping windows

nodes.label: Moving-block bootstrap confidence interval
nodes.rationale: Blocks of length at least the horizon preserve the autocorrelation a naive bootstrap destroys, so a directional-accuracy figure can be reported with an interval that answers whether it is distinguishable from 50%.

nodes.label: CRPS (continuous ranked probability score)
nodes.rationale: Strictly proper scoring rule for a full predictive distribution, approximable by averaging pinball loss across quantiles; a single comparable number is what makes a future comparison against a foundation-model baseline meaningful.

nodes.label: Winkler / interval score
nodes.rationale: Scores an interval on coverage AND width in one figure, which is the diagnosis coverage alone structurally cannot give: a band can hit nominal coverage by being enormous. It separated PYQ-247's arms by three orders of magnitude (64.3 vs 0.08). alpha is derived from the configured quantiles rather than assumed 0.2.

nodes.label: PIT histogram
nodes.rationale: Probability-integral transform of actuals through the predictive CDF: uniform means calibrated, U-shaped overconfident, hump-shaped underconfident. Values are computed, aggregated and serialized, but the chart itself is explicitly deferred.

nodes.label: Pinball loss and per-quantile exceedance
nodes.rationale: Outermost-band coverage is the least informative calibration statistic available: it cannot distinguish a calibrated band from one too wide on one side and too narrow on the other. Per-quantile exceedance tells you which side is wrong; pinball loss is the rule the model is actually trained on and is comparable across configs in a way val_loss (reported on normalized targets) is not.

nodes.label: 99.3%-coverage-on-nominal-80% band pathology
nodes.rationale: An 80% band containing 99% of outcomes is useless for decisions and silently collapses scan's band-direction guard into permanent HOLD. Turned out to be substantially a symptom of the non-stationary level target rather than an independent defect.

nodes.label: TTL panel cache and named dataset pins
nodes.rationale: Cache keyed by a fingerprint of (symbol, date range, enabled sources) with a TTL-exempt --pin NAME snapshot that replays byte-identical data later; TTL only gates read validity, so pruning needed its own command.
nodes.norm_label: ttl panel cache and named dataset pins

nodes.label: Provenance block in meta.json / runs.jsonl
nodes.rationale: Records pyquant version, git sha, pin name and resolved config. Not hypothetical: a bug redefined what RSI_14 means, so two bundles with identical feature names can have been trained on different data.

nodes.label: Reproducibility: seed + pinned data + code version
nodes.rationale: Seed alone does not reproduce a run; the missing third leg was code version. Also, seed_everything does not by itself guarantee determinism on every backend (cuDNN autotuning, non-deterministic reductions, num_workers>0 ordering), so the property was tested rather than assumed - it holds exactly on CPU, and GPU determinism is documented as unverified rather than implied.
nodes.norm_label: reproducibility: seed + pinned data + code version

nodes.label: Pipeline-spanning invariants
nodes.rationale: The backlog was optimising local correctness ticket by ticket while the invariants that span the pipeline went unstated. Six leak bugs were each correct in every individual file and wrong across files, so per-ticket regression tests prevent those three exact recurrences but not the next family member. Stating the invariants once, as properties rather than regressions, makes any future violating change fail regardless of which file it touched.

nodes.label: Learnability test with a degenerate noise control
nodes.rationale: Every existing roundtrip assertion would pass against a model that emits a constant. With a negative headline number there was no way to distinguish 'the target is not forecastable' from 'the wiring is silently broken'. Injecting a known learnable signal discriminates the two in seconds; the white-noise control catches the opposite failure, since a pipeline that finds skill in noise has a leak and this finds it without knowing where.
nodes.norm_label: learnability test with a degenerate noise control

nodes.label: A tool must earn its place against doing nothing
nodes.rationale: Recurring disposition inherited from the mypy decision: run the tool once, look at what it actually found, then decide whether it is a gate, a local convenience, or a no. Applied to decline MLflow (a 114-line runs.jsonl reader cannot drift from the source of truth and costs no dependencies), to gate ruff D (19 real gaps, zero ongoing maintenance), to defer ruff format as non-blocking, and to skip a fail_under coverage threshold.
nodes.norm_label: a tool must earn its place against doing nothing

nodes.label: Mocking at the transport boundary, not our own function boundary
nodes.rationale: Patching our own fetch_* functions verifies our logic against our own assumptions about the payload, which is half a test - it cannot catch the vendor changing response shape. Recorded real payloads paid for themselves immediately: yfinance returns Dividends/Stock Splits alongside OHLCV, and FRED attaches an entire historical series (26,321 rows) to the earliest vintage boundary. Complementary to the nightly live job: fixtures catch our regressions, the nightly catches theirs.
nodes.norm_label: mocking at the transport boundary, not our own function boundary

nodes.label: PriceProvider protocol and vendor abstraction
nodes.rationale: yfinance is an unofficial, unversioned, ToS-ambiguous scraper that is the sole source of OHLCV, VIX, sector ETFs and options - everything degrades gracefully except the one thing everything depends on. Two properties matter more than the vendor chosen: an interface so switching is config not rewrite, and an executable schema contract applied to whatever a provider returns so a subtly different frame fails at the boundary instead of misaligning a join three modules downstream. Tiingo chosen over Alpha Vantage (25 req/day) and Polygon/EODHD (paid), and needs no new dependency.

nodes.label: AUTO_ADJUST price-adjustment convention
nodes.rationale: Whether Close is split/dividend adjusted was decided by whichever yfinance version resolved, and it changes every price level, every derived indicator and therefore every trained model. True is the right convention because an unadjusted series has discontinuities that are not real price moves and every indicator would read them as ones. Stated once as a module constant rather than four files disagreeing.

nodes.label: ALFRED release vintages instead of fixed publication lags
nodes.rationale: A constant publication lag is an approximation in three ways: real release calendars vary, it handles only the first release while macro series are revised (so a 2019 training row sees today's revised number - look-ahead a date shift cannot fix at all), and it needs a hand-maintained constant per series. Vintage retrieval makes the constants unnecessary rather than merely more accurate and generalises to any new series for free.
nodes.norm_label: alfred release vintages instead of fixed publication lags

nodes.label: Structural-missingness indicator columns
nodes.rationale: At period=5y roughly 80% of rows carry a structural Sentiment=0 meaning 'no data', while at prediction time 0 means 'neutral news' - a textbook train/serve distribution shift on a feature, and only the second meaning ever occurs live. The flag marks coverage, not per-day presence: keying it off 'did this row have a headline' would collapse the two meanings the column exists to separate. The same shape of problem recurs for accumulated options history.

nodes.label: Selection-event bias and held-out reporting
nodes.rationale: Every trial in a search is a selection event, so a search of N trials inflates the best observed score; the winning configuration must be reported on a period the search never saw, with the in-search score explicitly labelled optimistically biased. The same caution applies to tuning signal thresholds on the data they are evaluated on.

nodes.label: Bundle feature-schema check
nodes.rationale: Bundles record their feature list and data-config toggles; read-side commands restore those toggles rather than starting from fresh defaults, and doctor turns 'your bundle is broken' from a runtime error into a proactive, deliberately offline check.

nodes.label: Signal P&L evaluation vs. forecast accuracy
nodes.rationale: Accuracy and usefulness are different questions: a model can have excellent MAE and a useless signal (right about magnitude, wrong about the sign that matters), or mediocre MAE and a profitable one. Scored conditional on a signal firing rather than on all days, with turnover and a per-trade cost that is usually decisive at daily frequency. Only informative once the band is calibrated, since the band-direction guard essentially never fires at 99% coverage.
nodes.norm_label: signal p&l evaluation vs. forecast accuracy

nodes.label: Options snapshot accumulation as a proprietary dataset
nodes.rationale: Put/call ratio, ATM IV and IV skew are the only forward-looking, market-priced signals in the data layer, and they were fetched, printed once and thrown away - because yfinance exposes only a current chain, so no historical IV series can be built from it. Appending a daily snapshot is useless on day one and a genuinely proprietary dataset after a year; the value is time-dependent, which is what makes starting now the highest value-per-effort option. Joined forward-filled with a neutral fill and an indicator rather than the panel's generic ffill+dropna, which would drop nearly the entire training window.
nodes.norm_label: options snapshot accumulation as a proprietary dataset

nodes.label: FastAPI service layer additive to the CLI
nodes.rationale: analysis/, models/ and data/ are already fully decoupled from Typer and Rich, so a REST layer is additive rather than a rewrite. Response models are constructed directly from the CLI's own serializers, which makes field-for-field parity true by construction instead of two independently-typed schemas that happen to agree today.
nodes.norm_label: fastapi service layer additive to the cli

nodes.label: In-process background jobs and where they stop scaling
nodes.rationale: Training blocks for the full fit, so it needs a job model; FastAPI BackgroundTasks plus a status endpoint is enough for a single node, and the stopping point is named explicitly (no queue, no retries, job state lost on restart) as the trigger to move to arq/RQ/Celery + Redis. Local-disk bundles are fine for one instance; multi-instance needs object storage.
nodes.norm_label: in-process background jobs and where they stop scaling

nodes.label: Per-bundle lock + LRU bundle cache
nodes.rationale: Serializes predict() against a given loaded model without blocking requests for different bundles, and a bounded LRU cache avoids re-paying checkpoint deserialization and a weights_only=False unpickle per request.

nodes.label: Never make a metric look better without making the model better
nodes.rationale: Applied repeatedly: directional accuracy dropping 80% to 52-56% under the log-return target is reported as the honest number because the old figure was flattered by the formulation; a +36.2% backtest is published beside the -23.5% headline rather than substituted for it because it is not the same measurement; defaults are not flipped on a sample of effective n about 5; acceptance criteria that could not be executed are recorded as verified-in-part rather than claimed whole.
nodes.norm_label: never make a metric look better without making the model better

nodes.label: Sphinx + intersphinx chosen over MkDocs
nodes.rationale: The codebase is largely a thin, correct layer over pandas / torch / pytorch-forecasting / pydantic, so resolving upstream types into live links carries real explanatory weight and mkdocstrings does not match intersphinx on this. autodoc_mock_imports was rejected for the same reason: mocked imports silently produce wrong signatures for anything inspecting a base class. A CPU-wheel install (1.2 GB vs 5.2 GB) is the middle path.

nodes.label: Scheduled checks are a notification, not a merge gate
nodes.rationale: A separate workflow beats a continue-on-error step inside CI, because a job in ci.yml appears on every PR's check list even when non-blocking, and a check permanently allowed to be red is a check people stop reading. Live vendor checks assert shape and freshness only, never values; the live smoke test lives inline in the workflow rather than tests/, since a live test in tests/ is one -k away from breaking the offline guarantee.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled checks are a notification, not a merge gate

nodes.label: Time-series foundation model as a third baseline
nodes.rationale: Persistence leaves the central question unanswered: is the TFT - 25 features, four vendors, a training loop, a bundle format - earning its complexity against something that needs none of it? Chronos-2 and TimesFM give probabilistic zero-shot forecasts with no training, features or API key, and all three possible outcomes are informative.
nodes.norm_label: time-series foundation model as a third baseline

nodes.label: Optuna study over six coupled hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Learning rate is one of at least six coupled knobs, so tuning it in isolation is close to uninformative. Two prerequisites: land the return target first, or a large search burns GPU hours discovering nothing helps inside a near-unbeatable formulation; and report the winner on a held-out period the search never saw. Two undocumented runtime requirements of pytorch-forecasting's optimize_hyperparameters were recorded inline: it unconditionally builds a TensorBoardLogger and adds a LearningRateMonitor, so tensorboard is required and trainer_kwargs must not set logger=False.
nodes.norm_label: optuna study over six coupled hyperparameters

nodes.label: Per-window dispersion beats a mean
nodes.rationale: A mean directional accuracy of 60% built from windows at 100/20/100/40/40 says something very different from five windows at 60%. Only became meaningful once the walk-forward genuinely walked - before that every origin evaluated the same final window and the spread would have reflected model-init noise. Level-target per-window skill [+0.28,+0.47,+0.35,-2.71,-3.13] is the case in point.

nodes.label: Global CLI options (--verbose/--debug/--format/--quiet)
nodes.rationale: Options belong to the application rather than a command, so they precede the command name. --format json implies --quiet so that piping into jq works without stripping ANSI escapes.

nodes.label: CLI exit-code taxonomy (0/1/2)
nodes.rationale: 1 means PyQuant ran and the data or bundle was wrong; 2 means the command line itself was wrong. The distinction matters in scripts. Failure paths assert non-zero exits rather than only success - the gap that PYQ-120 was.

nodes.label: pyquant train command
nodes.rationale: Reported metrics come from the best checkpoint, not the live post-fit model, because early stopping means the final epoch's weights are usually not the ones being scored (invariant 11).

nodes.label: Named dataset pin (TTL-exempt panel snapshot)
nodes.rationale: Pins are exempt from the cache TTL, which is what makes an experiment replayable months later - one of the three legs of reproducibility alongside the seed and the recorded code version. cache prune never touches pins; that is the entire point of a pin being a separate concept from a cache entry.

nodes.label: Pooling is not a free win (measured worse)
nodes.rationale: On an AAPL+ARM comparison (investigations.md#pyq-315) the pooled model scored worse than training each symbol alone. One comparison, one pair - directional, not settled - but enough that the README no longer states pooling's benefit as a rationale.
nodes.norm_label: pooling is not a free win (measured worse)

nodes.label: pyquant backtest command (walk-forward)
nodes.rationale: Each origin trains up to its own cutoff and scores the window starting at cutoff+1; consecutive origins evaluate disjoint windows. A five-window backtest is 25 predictions with an effective sample size around 5 because overlapping horizons are not independent draws - which is why the docs carry a +36.2% result without promoting it over the 280-prediction headline.

nodes.label: Per-trade round-trip cost in basis points
nodes.rationale: Default 5.0 bps applied to signal P&L: a signal that is only profitable at zero cost is not a signal.
nodes.norm_label: per-trade round-trip cost in basis points

nodes.label: pyquant tune command (Optuna search)
nodes.rationale: Every trial selects on the same data, so the winner is retrained and scored on a held-out period no trial ever saw; that number is reported rather than the in-search validation loss, which is optimistically biased by construction. Default 5 epochs per trial - trials are meant to be cheap and comparative, not converged.

nodes.label: pyquant forecast command
nodes.rationale: Every predicted step is strictly beyond the last observed bar, and the dates in the table, JSON, PNG and appended rows are one set (invariants 3, 4, 14). Non-monotonic bands are reordered for display and the count reported as n_quantile_crossings rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Options snapshot is display-only, never a model input
nodes.rationale: The options snapshot is printed as live market context when use_options is on but is never fed to the model.
nodes.norm_label: options snapshot is display-only, never a model input

nodes.label: pyquant explain command
nodes.rationale: Prints a caveat when the bundle's recorded skill is non-positive: attributing importance within a model that does not beat persistence tells you what the model leaned on, not what moves the price. Permutation importance and the TFT's variable-selection weights agree only on the top feature (Spearman rho ~ 0.3) - investigations.md#pyq-314.

nodes.label: pyquant scan command
nodes.rationale: One symbol failing does not sink the run: untrained comes back as not_trained and failing as error, each as its own row. The signal classifier and row shape are shared with the HTTP API's POST /scan so the two front-ends cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: pyquant snapshot command (options history accrual)
nodes.rationale: yfinance exposes only a current option chain, never history, so running this on a schedule is the only way the project can ever build a historical options-implied series (OptionsPutCallRatio, OptionsATMIV, OptionsIVSkew).

nodes.label: pyquant doctor command
nodes.rationale: Exits non-zero if any bundle's feature schema can no longer be satisfied, turning a broken bundle into something you find by asking rather than by a forecast failing three weeks later. Key presence is reported; key values never are.

nodes.label: pyquant cache list/prune/rm-pin
nodes.rationale: A cached panel is never replayed across a feature redefinition: the cache key fingerprints the feature set, so a redefinition misses rather than serving a stale panel under a new meaning (invariant 15).

nodes.label: CLI --format json output contract
nodes.rationale: Every serializer lives in pyquant.analysis.serialize - the same module the HTTP API builds its responses from, so a CLI document and an API response come from one implementation rather than two schemas that happen to agree today. Fields requiring configuration are omitted rather than raising.

nodes.label: Forecast dates are shipped, never re-derived
nodes.rationale: A consumer should not have to rebuild an exchange calendar - holidays included - to find out which day a prediction is for.
nodes.norm_label: forecast dates are shipped, never re-derived

nodes.label: Every rate carries its denominator (invariant 12)
nodes.rationale: evaluation_to_dict emits each sample count next to the rate it describes, so a directional accuracy is never readable without the number of points behind it. It exists because this project once reported 'directional accuracy 100.0%' off five points.

nodes.label: FastAPI service layer design note (PYQ-213)
nodes.rationale: Kept as-is after implementation (PYQ-261) because the implementation followed it directly; this page is the reasoning, http-api.md is the interface.

nodes.label: Additive second front-end, not a rewrite
nodes.rationale: The analysis/model/data layers are already fully decoupled from Typer/Rich and cli/app.py is a thin caller over plain functions returning plain dataclasses, so a FastAPI app wraps exactly those same functions and nothing in the core has to move.
nodes.norm_label: additive second front-end, not a rewrite

nodes.label: pyquant/api/ package layout
nodes.rationale: app.py / schemas.py / deps.py / jobs.py / routes/, behind an optional api extra so the base install stays lean.

nodes.label: Pydantic response models at the API boundary
nodes.rationale: Numpy is the sharp edge: every np.ndarray/np.float64 must be converted or JSON encoding fails, so conversion is centralized at the boundary and the API contract stays decoupled from internal dataclass changes.
nodes.norm_label: pydantic response models at the api boundary

nodes.label: Shared serializers between CLI and API (PYQ-212 first)
nodes.rationale: Implement domain-to-JSON-able-dict functions once, have the CLI print them and the API return them; build PYQ-212 first so numpy-to-JSON logic is never duplicated, then wrap in thin pydantic models purely for OpenAPI schema generation.
nodes.norm_label: shared serializers between cli and api (pyq-212 first)

nodes.label: Training as a background job (202 + job id)
nodes.rationale: tft.train() blocks for a full Lightning fit - seconds on synthetic data, minutes or longer on real 5y panels - so a request thread must not block on it.
nodes.norm_label: training as a background job (202 + job id)

nodes.label: In-process job registry (v1 scaffold)
nodes.rationale: A dict[str, JobRecord] guarded by a lock, updated by the background task on completion - good enough for one instance and low training concurrency.

nodes.label: Triggers to graduate to a real job queue
nodes.rationale: Job state in process memory is lost on restart and invisible to a second instance; no concurrency control means two large fits can OOM; no retries, backpressure, scheduling or cancellation; BackgroundTasks shares the event loop so a CPU-bound fit needs a worker pool anyway. Move to arq or Celery+Redis the moment you need durable jobs, more than one instance, or bounded training concurrency.
nodes.norm_label: triggers to graduate to a real job queue

nodes.label: Bundle storage backend decision (local disk vs object storage)
nodes.rationale: Multi-instance breaks local disk: the box that served POST /train is not necessarily the one serving GET /forecast later. Prerequisites regardless of backend are PYQ-220 (absolute checkpoint/cache paths - a server's CWD is not the repo root) and a load_bundle/save_bundle abstraction so local-vs-S3 is one swap rather than scattered Path joins.
nodes.norm_label: bundle storage backend decision (local disk vs object storage)

nodes.label: Measured forecast latency profile (PYQ-319)
nodes.rationale: AAPL, default period=5y: cold total ~65.4 s of which fetch+panel-build is 64.3 s (98%); predict() is 812 ms cold / 632 ms warm; warm total ~0.84 s. Caveat: one symbol, one run, live vendor latency at 2026-07-27 - the qualitative conclusion is robust, the millisecond figures are not.

nodes.label: Panel cache hit rate decides perceived service latency
nodes.rationale: The forward pass is not the bottleneck. The LRU bundle cache saves ~250-450 ms; a panel cache or background pre-warm saves ~64 s. FRED's 15 requests per cold call at the default period means an operator serving many distinct symbols cold hits the FRED rate limit long before CPU or GPU does.
nodes.norm_label: panel cache hit rate decides perceived service latency

nodes.label: Per-bundle prediction lock (design)
nodes.rationale: TemporalFusionTransformer.predict() is not safe to call concurrently on the same model instance - pytorch-forecasting spins up an internal Lightning Trainer per call and mutates model state. Serialize per model; parallelism across different bundles is fine, and torch intra-op threading already uses multiple cores so the cost is lower than it sounds.

nodes.label: In-process LRU cache of ModelBundle (design)
nodes.rationale: Reloading per request pays checkpoint deserialization every time and re-triggers the weights_only=False unpickle (PYQ-306). Bounded size caps memory; entries are invalidated when the bundle is retrained.

nodes.label: Long-running server is where schema drift bites (PYQ-302)
nodes.rationale: 'Source enabled at train time, rate-limited at predict time' is exactly the server case; unresolved, a transient upstream outage yields malformed predictions rather than a clean error. The design also depends on the FinBERT cache fix (PYQ-114), which memoizes only on success so a transient first-request failure no longer disables sentiment for the process lifetime.
nodes.norm_label: long-running server is where schema drift bites (pyq-302)

nodes.label: API-key gate as a FastAPI dependency (design)
nodes.rationale: A public endpoint would spend the operator's FRED/Finnhub/Yahoo quota on every caller. Keys from config/secret store, constant-time compare, 401 on failure; never echo upstream API keys in responses or logs.
nodes.norm_label: api-key gate as a fastapi dependency (design)

nodes.label: Per-key rate limiting (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Training especially must be tightly capped since it is expensive and quota-hungry; slowapi or the reverse-proxy/API-gateway layer are the candidate places.

nodes.label: Deployment shape (CPU image for serving, CUDA for training)
nodes.rationale: A CPU-only image is enough for forecast/explain/scan; training wants CUDA. Built via uv sync --frozen --extra api, entry point uvicorn pyquant.api.app:app. Pairs with PYQ-217.
nodes.norm_label: deployment shape (cpu image for serving, cuda for training)

nodes.label: Recommended API build order
nodes.rationale: Serializers (PYQ-212) then absolute paths (PYQ-220) before any endpoint, read-only endpoints before /train, Dockerfile before deploy, and object storage plus a Redis queue only if and when multi-instance or durability is actually needed.

nodes.label: Development guide
nodes.rationale: Nothing needs a GPU, an API key, or network access; the two CI gates (ruff check, backlog.py check) are the same commands a contributor runs locally.

nodes.label: Network-free test suite
nodes.rationale: Every external call is mocked so pytest passes offline; real vendor payloads are checked in as fixtures instead, refreshed by record_fixtures.py.

nodes.label: Behaviour-named tests
nodes.rationale: The name states the property being asserted, so a failure report reads as a claim that stopped holding.

nodes.label: Test-first for bug fixes
nodes.rationale: Not ceremony: writing failure-path tests for the CLI found two real defects success-path tests could not have, because 18 of those tests asserted exit_code == 0 and therefore tested nothing about failure.

nodes.label: Assert the invariant, not the output
nodes.rationale: A test pinned to a number breaks on every legitimate change and catches nothing structural.
nodes.norm_label: assert the invariant, not the output

nodes.label: Never weaken a test to make it pass
nodes.rationale: If a test starts failing, the default assumption is that the code broke. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test.
nodes.norm_label: never weaken a test to make it pass

nodes.label: scripts/ research tooling
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not part of the test suite - most need network, some need hours - but they are how each measured result is reproduced rather than taken on trust.

nodes.label: scripts/compare_pooling.py
nodes.rationale: Scores a pooled model on each symbol's own validation slice separately, which train()'s aggregated metric cannot do. Reported in investigations.md#pyq-315.

nodes.label: scripts/ablate_features.py
nodes.rationale: Walk-forward backtests across cumulative feature groups plus a correlation matrix naming the redundant technicals. Reported in investigations.md#pyq-316 and bugs.md#pyq-140.

nodes.label: scripts/profile_forecast.py
nodes.rationale: Times a cold and a warm forecast call split into bundle-load / fetch+panel-build / predict. Reported in investigations.md#pyq-319 and the API design note.

nodes.label: scripts/runs.py compare
nodes.rationale: Reads every bundle's runs.jsonl and lines the fields up. It is also an argument in itself: the ~100-line alternative shipped instead of taking on mlflow as a dependency.

nodes.label: scripts/record_fixtures.py
nodes.rationale: Refreshes the checked-in vendor payloads the contract tests read; article text is replaced with placeholders because the tests care about response shape, not copyrighted copy.

nodes.label: scripts/backlog.py check|list
nodes.rationale: Backlog consistency and priority-sorted open tickets; no dependencies, runs from a bare clone.

nodes.label: New dependencies need a recorded reason
nodes.rationale: mypy in CI and a real-FinBERT CI job were both declined on measured evidence, and that disposition is a feature.
nodes.norm_label: new dependencies need a recorded reason

nodes.label: backlog/ as source of truth
nodes.rationale: IDs never move between files and tickets never move within a file - only the Status line changes - which is what makes 'see PYQ-109' a permanent link. Enforced by backlog.py check, not stylistic.

nodes.label: Resolution note standard
nodes.rationale: Not a changelog entry: it states behaviour change, the decision made, verification evidence with real before/after numbers, the guarding tests, and what the fix invalidates elsewhere. These notes are why the docs can cite a ticket instead of restating an argument.

nodes.label: Building the docs site
nodes.rationale: --extra api is required, not optional: pyquant/api/ imports fastapi at module level, autodoc imports every module it documents, and fail_on_warning would fail the whole build over one section most readers never open. Colour tokens live in conf.py theme options and structure in _static/custom.css so a value is defined once per theme.

nodes.label: Docs built with -W --keep-going
nodes.rationale: A docs site not built with warnings-as-errors rots within two refactors: a renamed module, a dead :func: reference or an autodoc import failure all degrade silently otherwise. A nightly job re-resolves intersphinx inventories so an upstream removal is caught by a scheduled run rather than by a reader.

nodes.label: Never make a metric look better without making the model better
nodes.rationale: The project's credibility rests on having replaced 'directional accuracy 100.0%' with an honest '57.5% on 280 points'. If a past number turns out wrong, say so loudly and supersede the tickets that relied on it.
nodes.norm_label: never make a metric look better without making the model better

nodes.label: Look-ahead leakage is the top risk
nodes.rationale: Every leak found so far was correct in each individual file and wrong across files. Before any change to data/ or split geometry ask whether a row at time t can now see information that did not exist at time t; twice, 'what does decoder_time_idx actually contain' was the entire bug.
nodes.norm_label: look-ahead leakage is the top risk

nodes.label: Every claim must be measured, not expected
nodes.rationale: A rationale for why something should help is not a result. Pooling was described that way once; it is now a measured - and corrected - claim.
nodes.norm_label: every claim must be measured, not expected

nodes.label: Comments explain why and cite ticket IDs
nodes.rationale: The convention is how the code and the backlog stay connected; there are dozens of such references across pyquant/.
nodes.norm_label: comments explain why and cite ticket ids

nodes.label: HTTP API guide
nodes.rationale: A FastAPI service over the same analysis/ and models/ calls the CLI makes (PYQ-261); additive because cli/app.py was already a mapping from command to a plain function returning a plain dataclass.

nodes.label: X-API-Key authentication (shipped)
nodes.rationale: Comparison is constant-time so response timing cannot leak a valid key one byte at a time. Keys come from the environment rather than Settings deliberately: a Settings field can end up in meta.json, a log line or a cache fingerprint, and key values never do. An unconfigured service fails loudly with 500 rather than falling open.

nodes.label: HTTP endpoint surface (v1)
nodes.rationale: Symbols are upper-cased on the way in so /forecast/aapl and /forecast/AAPL are the same bundle.

nodes.label: HTTP status-code taxonomy (401/404/409/422/500)
nodes.rationale: FeatureSchemaMismatch maps to 409, a conflict rather than a server error: the model is fine, the world moved.

nodes.label: GET /forecast/{symbol}
nodes.rationale: ForecastResponse is constructed directly from serialize.forecast_to_dict - the same function behind 'pyquant --format json forecast' - so forecast_dates and n_quantile_crossings are present for the same reasons.

nodes.label: POST /scan
nodes.rationale: Returns 200 even when individual symbols fail; each row carries status ok/not_trained/error. Same scan_row_to_dict implementation as the CLI so signal and band_width_pct cannot drift between front-ends.

nodes.label: POST /train and GET /train/{job_id}
nodes.rationale: Training takes minutes so POST /train returns 202 immediately; status moves queued -> running -> succeeded|failed.

nodes.label: Bundle-cache eviction after a successful train job
nodes.rationale: Without evicting the retrained bundle, a cached copy from before the run would keep serving the old weights to the next /forecast or /explain.
nodes.norm_label: bundle-cache eviction after a successful train job

nodes.label: Shipped concurrency model
nodes.rationale: Both mechanisms come from measured behaviour rather than assumption: a cold call is ~98% vendor fetch and panel build (~65 s) and the forward pass is under a second either way, so optimising the model path would have been optimising 2% of the wall clock.

nodes.label: LRU cache of 8 loaded bundles (shipped)
nodes.rationale: Loading is real file I/O plus checkpoint deserialisation; the load happens outside the cache lock so loading one bundle does not block requests for bundles already resident.

nodes.label: One lock per bundle (shipped)
nodes.rationale: predict() is unsafe concurrently on one model instance because pytorch-forecasting spins up an internal Lightning Trainer per call and mutates model state. Different bundles proceed in parallel; the cost is low because torch already uses multiple cores within a call.

nodes.label: What API v1 deliberately does not do
nodes.rationale: In-process job registry, per-process bundle cache, local-filesystem bundles, no rate limiting. These are documented triggers to graduate rather than defects to file: cheap to live with for a single instance and wrong to pretend away for more than one.
nodes.norm_label: what api v1 deliberately does not do

nodes.label: Configuration reference
nodes.rationale: Every tunable lives on one of four pydantic models; the 'config over constants' convention exists because hardcoded literals in models/tft.py generated four separate tickets.

nodes.label: Settings precedence chain
nodes.rationale: CLI flags > env > .env > YAML > defaults. YAML sits deliberately below the environment so a checked-in experiment config stays overridable per-run, and explicit CLI flags applied after load_settings() win over everything. Nested values use a double-underscore delimiter.

nodes.label: A missing --config path is an error, not a silent fallback
nodes.rationale: The underlying settings source treats a missing file as 'no values to contribute', so a typo used to train a completely different experiment than the one asked for - and record it in meta.json as such.
nodes.norm_label: a missing --config path is an error, not a silent fallback

nodes.label: Field descriptions read out of pyquant/config.py
nodes.rationale: An explicit Field(description=...) if set, otherwise the # comment attached to that field. Fields with a blank description have no explanation in the source; that gap is reported rather than papered over with invented prose.
nodes.norm_label: field descriptions read out of pyquant/config.py

nodes.label: Key presence recorded, key values never
nodes.rationale: Secrets are optional and their absence disables the corresponding enrichment. Presence is recorded in cache fingerprints and meta.json; values never are - not in logs, not in runs.jsonl, not in a fingerprint.
nodes.norm_label: key presence recorded, key values never

nodes.label: TrainingConfig.validation_days
nodes.rationale: Window count is validation_days - max_prediction_length + 1, so a holdout of exactly one horizon yields a single window: five points driving every reported metric plus early stopping and checkpoint selection. That is where the discarded 'directional accuracy 100.0%' came from.

nodes.label: purge_horizon / embargo_days
nodes.rationale: Look-ahead control around every split; they shrink the training slice only, never the scored window (invariant 10).

nodes.label: TrainingConfig.target (close vs log_return)
nodes.rationale: 'close' predicts the price level; 'log_return' predicts per-step log returns and reconstructs a price path for display. The default is deliberately conservative, and the choice matters more than any hyperparameter here.

nodes.label: TFTConfig.quantiles must be sorted and contain 0.5
nodes.rationale: Validated rather than assumed: the first and last entries are the lower and upper calibration bounds, so an unsorted list like [0.9, 0.1, 0.5] would silently invert the band with no error. 0.5 must be present because every consumer of a forecast reads a median.
nodes.norm_label: tftconfig.quantiles must be sorted and contain 0.5

nodes.label: Enrichment flag is a request, not an assertion
nodes.rationale: A source activates only if enabled and holding the credentials and data it needs; otherwise it degrades gracefully with a logged notice. The contract holds for training and deliberately stops at predict time. use_options gates a display-only fetch - the options snapshot is never a model feature.
nodes.norm_label: enrichment flag is a request, not an assertion

nodes.label: API reference index (autosummary)
nodes.rationale: One page per public module generated from docstrings; the docstrings are the point because they cite ticket IDs, explain why a default is what it is, and record decisions.

nodes.label: Why pyquant.config gets a hand-built page
nodes.rationale: pydantic v2 moves model fields off the class at class-creation time, so plain autodoc renders each one as a bare name: type with neither its default nor the comment explaining it.
nodes.norm_label: why pyquant.config gets a hand-built page

nodes.label: Documented layer map (config/data/models/analysis/cli/api)
nodes.rationale: models/tft.py is the only module besides data/dataset.py that imports pytorch-forecasting or Lightning; analysis/ is library-agnostic (plain numpy arrays and dataclasses, no torch, no Typer, no Rich); cli/ is a thin caller; api/ is a second front-end over the same layers.

nodes.label: Intersphinx upstream type resolution
nodes.rationale: This codebase is largely a thin, correct layer over pandas/numpy/torch/pytorch_forecasting/pydantic, so knowing exactly which TimeSeriesDataSet or DataFrame a function returns carries real explanatory weight. Runtime type objects stringify to their defining module (pandas.core.frame.DataFrame) rather than the documented public name, so conf.py maps the former onto the latter before giving up.

nodes.label: nitpicky is deliberately off (PYQ-233)
nodes.rationale: Turning it on would make every unresolvable type reference an error, but a large share of remaining unresolved names are upstream types whose inventories do not publish them - noisy rather than informative. The build already runs under -W --keep-going, so a broken cross-reference in this project's own docstrings fails the build today.

nodes.label: Private helpers omitted from the reference
nodes.rationale: _prediction_dataset, _evaluate_validation, _window_validation_dataset and friends carry some of the densest reasoning in the codebase; read them in the source or via the [source] links on each page.
nodes.norm_label: private helpers omitted from the reference

nodes.label: autosummary module template
nodes.rationale: Renders each module page with :member-order: bysource, so generated pages follow the reading order the author chose in the file rather than alphabetical order.
